title: China's Z.ai disables AI coding assistant features after security issue

reading.body:
This is a data egress failure in a developer tool, not a model error. A feature that shipped enabled by default sent local code repositories to a cloud service, and the developers whose machines held those repositories had not agreed to it. The failure sits in the default configuration of a deployed product, at the point where a local file leaves the user's environment.

Catching it would have required treating the default setting as the decision it is. A tool that reads local source code and transmits it needs the transmission to be off until the user turns it on, or disclosed at the moment it happens. The upload path was disabled only after developers reported it, which places detection outside the vendor.

What is not established is whether any code data was retained. Z.ai said independent reviews found none, which is a company statement rather than a finding reported here, and the claim that six workspaces of sensitive data were uploaded was retracted by the company that made it. Intent is not established either.

reports.title: China's Z.ai disables AI coding assistant features after security issue

summary: Developers reported that Z.ai's ZCode AI coding assistant uploaded local code repositories to Alibaba Cloud without consent. Z.ai said a Codebase Indexing feature that was enabled by default caused this. The company apologized, fixed the vulnerability, and later disabled the upload path. One company retracted a separate claim that six workspaces containing sensitive data had been uploaded. Z.ai said independent reviews found no code data was retained.
title_en: China's Z.ai disables AI coding assistant features after security issue
